| [0010](./0010/) | core | accepted | major | in-progress | 2026-08-12 — D30'S STRIP IMPLEMENTATION LANDED — in 0011's library-compat-comparator slice, not in this entry's library-matching, and the placement is a recorded scope addition against this plan rather than a drift. The mechanism is exactly D30's: denylist of metadata.catalogVersion + metadata.description, syntax round-trip via Syntax(cue.All(), cue.InlineImports(true)) -> AST delete from every metadata block -> rebuild, reaching the definition as well as the instance (the required-field leftover Validate(cue.Concrete(false)) cannot flag), closedness preserved, InlineImports proven required by a fixture that fails without it. The known position-loss cost carries over as accepted. WHY THERE: the comparator is unusable without the strip — catalogVersion changes on every release by construction, so an unstripped gate fires on every publish — and shipping it once in opm/compat, the package both consumers import, avoids two implementations of a subtle AST transform. WHAT THIS ENTRY IS STILL OWED: library-matching's unify-rung APPLICATION of the strip is unmoved and still that slice's work, along with its D34 consumption of compat.CompareAPIVersions — the kube-aware total ordering also shipped in the same slice, parity-pinned to core #APIVersionType, fixing sortFQNsBySemVer's measured non-transitive triple. The same landing unblocks library-acquire-and-subscription's move half: HighestStable now lives in opm/compat with materialize's filterVersions calling across the boundary, so D14's deletion of filter.go no longer strands predecessor selection. | Module and Catalog Identity |

| [0013](./0013/) | cross-cutting | draft | - | not-started | 2026-07-27 — Design revised on review: D10 supersedes D1, D11 supersedes D4, D12 amends D9, and OQ1 is closed. D1 had removed the `#Secret` contract type AND the disjunction inside it, when only the routing metadata needed to move to the attribute — leaving the deployer no slot in which to say "this Secret already exists", and forcing the handle-plus-context-map machinery of D4 to compensate. D10 restores `#Secret` narrowed to `#SecretLiteral | #SecretRef`, so the ATTRIBUTE carries routing (author intent, static, in the published module) and the TYPE carries fulfilment (deployer choice, per environment, type-checked by CUE). D11 replaces handle substitution with resolve-in-place: the kernel rewrites every secret to its `#SecretRef` form, so both arms converge before render, a transformer reads two fields from one branch, and the whole handle format, the `#TransformerContext` addition, the `owned` flag and the output scanner are all deleted. Three properties fall out that the first draft lacked: instance files for supplied secrets do not change at all, plaintext in the render is structurally unrepresentable rather than stripped, and a secret interpolated into a rendered string fails at plain `cue vet` at authoring time. Experiment 02 rebuilt as `02-resolve-in-place` and re-run: all five claims held, and its Go content hash agrees with the CUE one in examples.cue. OQ2 opened — whether the arm rewrite survives the real kernel build path — and is now the sole blocker to acceptance. | Attribute-Declared Secret Fields |

| [0015](./0015/) | cross-cutting | draft | - | not-started | 2026-08-05 — Drafted from a design conversation grounded in three measurements taken the same day. `core/src/catalog.cue` carries exactly ONE member map, `#transformers`, and `library/opm/materialize/index.go:39-41` skips any catalog build without one — so a contract with no adapter is absent from the materialized world, which is precisely the state 0010 D37's `fulfilment: "provider"` creates on purpose. `compile/match.go:344-360` is SUBSET containment, not equality, so a more-specific transformer never displaces a less-specific one; both pair and both render, and 0010 D32's guard does not reach the case because it fires only for `fulfilment: "provider"` contracts. And the real discriminator across the 8 transformers sharing `catalog_opm`'s `#ContainerResource` bucket is `requiredLabels` (`daemonset_transformer.cue:27-29`), not the resource/trait set — which is what makes 0010 D36's `matchLabels` the lever for provider classes rather than a new matcher concept. Four decisions locked: D1 (explicit contract maps), D2 (classes, amending 0010 D37), D3 (RBAC-gated registration CR), D4 (no contract/adapter packaging split, decided now because riding 0010's FQN break is nearly free and a standalone break later is not). Six Open Questions carried. | Catalog Contracts, Provider Classes, and Transformer Registration |

## Status legend

- **draft** — initial design, actively being written
- **accepted** — design agreed upon, ready for implementation
- **implemented** — design has been realized in code
- **superseded** — replaced by a newer enhancement (see `superseded_by` in the entry's config.yaml)
